decisions.reason: Having remained on the market and fitting tightly with our established psychiatric and therapeutic capabilities, the program likely meets aspiration levels well enough that an expanding organisation with some slack will continue it.

The carpentry workshop still supports our workshop and participation mission, but because it is more peripheral and commercially exposed than our core care services, it remains the product most likely to be dropped if results stay below aspirations.
As an outpatient service very close to our core support offer, sociotherapy is likely to be retained while we continue learning from demand and integration with existing care pathways.

The counseling service for senior living is closely aligned with our eldercare competencies and its earlier prominence suggests it has reached acceptable internal aspirations, making withdrawal unlikely.

Meal delivery for seniors fits our client base and service logic, but as a newer and less prominently positioned offer it still carries moderate uncertainty and would be reconsidered sooner than our more established care-linked additions if performance disappointed.
